newsitem.title: USA: Pa. rejects more money for Phila. schools - paper.
newsitem.headline: Pa. rejects more money for Phila. schools - paper.

text.p: Pennsylvania officials rejected a call from the Philadelphia School District for more aid to cover a growing budget deficit, Philadelphia Inquirer reported Thursday.
The state's Secretary of Education, Eugene Hickok, said city schools already receive more than their fair share of state education dollars.
Earlier this week, Philadelphia school district officials said the budget gap was $10.4 million in the current $1.4 billion budget, and warned that figure could grow to $104 million in fiscal 1998.

Local official called on the state to help close the gap, but Hickok said Pennsylvania's $682 million subsidy was enough. He said Philadelphia schools receive an average of $2,810 per pupil, compared to $423 in the five districts surrounding the city.
Local officials argued that Philadelphia has a disproportionate share of poor pupils.
